task: Propose one proportionate structural improvement from the supplied history, including how to prove it catches the failure and preserves valid uses. This is a proposal only; no repository or policy edits are authorized.
context: Incident A: a tenant-scoped item cache used item_id alone, allowing two tenants with item_id=7 to share a value. Incident B: another caller independently built a string key from item_id alone and reproduced the same cross-tenant collision. Both callers currently construct keys directly. Incident C: one request timed out during an unrelated network outage. There is also a global public-catalog cache whose identifiers are intentionally not tenant-scoped. No type system, linter, or language-specific tooling is assumed.
expected: Groups A and B as the supported repeated failure class and keeps C separate.
Proposes a shared tenant-aware boundary or similarly structural safeguard instead of only a reminder.
Defines a negative test with two tenants and the same item ID and a legitimate case preserving global catalog behavior.
Explains how enforcement scope or bypass handling prevents a superficial keyword rule from overreaching.
Labels all implementation and prevention claims as proposed until exercised.
forbidden: Mandating tenant identity for the explicitly global catalog cache.
Claiming an unimplemented safeguard already prevents the defect.
Treating the single unrelated timeout as evidence for the same recurring class.
evidence: Inspect the grouping, enforcement mechanism, concrete failing and valid cases, and distinction between proposal and proof.
